messages.author: 773b8742e60f5bfa
messages.subject: hurdle model for gamma distribution
parts:
Hi,

Probably it's not a new topic, but could not find the solution about a proper implement of hurdle method to truncated gamma distribution in Stan.
Following the manual, I came up with the model below. When I ran the model, I've got error message suggesting ill-conditioned or misspecified model.
Any comment/suggestion would be greatly appreciated.
Thanks.


data {
  int<lower=0> Ndata ;
  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[Ndata] y ; // data
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> a ; // shape
  real<lower=0> b ; // rate
  real<lower=0, upper=1> p ; // prob.
}
model {
    for (i in 1:Ndata) {
    (y[i] == 0) ~ bernoulli(p);
    if (y[i] > 0)
      y[i] ~ gamma(a, b) T[0,1];
    }
}

messages.author: 0839befa8a8b7d53
messages.subject: Re: hurdle model for gamma distribution
parts:
I've done gamma hurdle models in Stan. I constructed the data model like this:

if ( y[i] == 0 )
    increment_log_prob(bernoulli_log(1,p));
else
    increment_log_prob(bernoulli_log(0,p) + gamma_log(y[i],a,b));

Not exactly the same formulation as your code, I don't think.

But I suspect the issue is the lack of priors. a and b have flat priors on the support, so random start values for the gamma probability could be an issue. In my experience getting a gamma model going requires using tight priors or custom start values, especially if there's much dispersion in the data.

So maybe try some exponential priors on a and b and start values that you know evaluate to a finite likelihood?

messages.author: af66ceee430188cb
messages.subject: Re: hurdle model for gamma distribution
parts: Your y value is real and the Bernoulli distribution has support only on the integer set {0,1}. That would be my guess as to why the model gave a misspecification error. Richard's code gets around that problem, though.

messages.author: 89abf8a3796a510b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: hurdle model for gamma distribution
parts:
It's a good idea to use arrays for integer-valued data. so the data block would look like:

data {
  int<lower=0> Ndata ;
  int y[Ndata] ; // data
}


Rob
